'''Tsuchimikado Ariharu''' (土御門 有春) was a noble and {{ill|Onmyōji|fa|اونمیو-جی|ja|陰陽師|ko|음양사|vi|Âm Dương sư|zh|陰陽師|zh_yue|陰陽師|qid=Q2274163|lt=Onmyōji}} during the {{ill|Sengoku Period (Japan)|ja|戦国時代|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sengoku period (Japan)|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q117415390}}. He was the 29th head of the {{ill|Tsuchimikado clan|ja|土御門家 (安倍氏)|lt=Tsuchimikado family}}, a {{ill|Tōshōke|ja|堂上家|ko|당상가|zh|堂上家|zh_classical|堂上家|qid=Q11427847}} of the {{ill|Half-house (Kuge)|ja|半家|qid=Q11406995}} Rank in the {{ill|Abe clan|ja|阿倍氏}} lineage.

== Biography ==
Tsuchimikado Ariharu was the son of {{ill|Tsuchimikado Arisue|ja|土御門有季}}, who served as {{ill|Yin-Yang Bureau|ja|陰陽頭|lt=Onmyō no kami}}. 

In {{ill|Tenmon|ja|天文|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tenbun|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q21096812}} 12, on {{ill|July 28|en|July 28|qid=Q2718|lt=July 28 (old calendar)}} ({{ill|1543|en|1543|qid=Q6523|lt=1543}} {{ill|August 28|en|August 28|qid=Q2817|lt=August 28}}), he assumed the position of {{ill|Ministry of Ceremonies (Japan)|ja|治部卿|lt=Minister of Ceremonies|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ministry of Ceremonies (Japan)|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 治部省|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q10829855}}. His official Ranks included {{ill|Junior Third Rank|ja|従三位}}, {{ill|Yin-Yang Bureau|ja|陰陽頭|lt=Onmyō no kami}}, and {{ill|Hisanagi|ja|非参議}}.

During his tenure, the rival {{ill|Kamo clan|ja|賀茂朝臣氏}}, particularly the {{ill|Kadenokōji family|ja|勘解由小路家 (賀茂氏)}}, faced turmoil. {{ill|Kadenokōji Aritomi|ja|勘解由小路在富|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kadenokōji Akitomi|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q11400104}}, head of the Kadenokōji family, saw his son {{ill|Kamo Akimasa|ja|賀茂在昌}} abandon Kyoto with his family to study astronomy and Christianity in {{ill|Funai (Bungo Province)|ja|豊後府内}}. After Akitomi's death in {{ill|Eiroku|en|Eiroku|qid=Q1143341|lt=Eiroku}} 8 ({{ill|1565|en|1565|qid=Q6634|lt=1565}}), Ariharu's son {{ill|Kadenokōji Akitaka|ja|勘解由小路在高}} was adopted by the Kadenokōji family to preserve its lineage.
